(basketball)|Blocks]] | stat3value = 130 (1.2 bpg) }} '''Gregory Wayne Oden Jr.''' (born January 22, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Oden, a 7 ft 0 in (2.13 m) [[center (basketball)|center]],{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/201141/career|title=NBA.com/Stats|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 10, 2022}} played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]] for [[2006–07 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|one season]], during which the team was the [[2007 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten Conference regular season champion]] and [[2007 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] champion with Oden as the [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player|tournament MOP]]. Additionally, the Buckeyes were the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|tournament runner-up]] in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship records|NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/gallery/biggest-draft-busts-kwame-brown-michael-olowokandi-sam-bowie-darko-milicic-062512|title=Biggest draft busts in NBA history|date=October 20, 2016|website=foxsports.com|accessdate=January 4, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.thesportster.com/basketball/nba-draft-bust-disappointment-injuries/|title=The Biggest Bust In Each NBA Draft From The 2000s|date=May 4, 2020|website=TheSportster|accessdate=January 4, 2022}} On June 28, 2007, Oden was [[NBA first overall draft pick|selected first overall]] in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He underwent [[microfracture surgery]] of the knee in September 2007 and missed the entire [[2007–08 NBA season]] as a result. Oden recovered and made his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut on opening night 2008. In March 2012, he was waived by the Trail Blazers after missing the previous two seasons due to injuries.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7692811/source-portland-trail-blazers-waive-former-no-1-overall-pick-greg-oden |title=Blazers waive center Greg Oden |date=March 15, 2012 |author=ESPN.com news services |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=March 15, 2012}} Oden signed with the [[Miami Heat]] in August 2013, more than three years after last appearing in an NBA game, and played with the team through the [[2014 NBA playoffs]]. After playing in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] during its 2015–16 season, Oden stated in October 2016 that he was done with basketball and would not be returning as a player.{{cite news |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/espn/otl/story/_/id/18022504/greg-oden-says-remembered-biggest-bust-nba-history |title=Greg Oden: 'I'll be remembered as the biggest bust in NBA history' |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |website=[[ESPN]] |date=November 12, 2016}} In July 2018, he played in [[The Basketball Tournament 2018]].{{cite news |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2788264-greg-oden-goes-for-11-and-5-in-return-to-court-at-the-basketball-tournament |title=Greg Oden Goes for 11 and 5 in Return to Court at the Basketball Tournament |first=Alec |last=Nathan |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=July 27, 2018 |access-date=July 28, 2018}} In May 2019, Oden was selected as the seventh overall pick in the 2019 [[Big3]] Draft.{{cite news |url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball/2019/05/104015/greg-oden-selected-no-7-by-aliens-in-the-big3-expansion-draft |title=Greg Oden Selected No. 7 by Aliens in the BIG3 Draft |first=Kevin |last=Harrish |date=May 1, 2019 |access-date=July 6, 2019}} ==Early years== Oden was born on January 22, 1988, in [[Buffalo, New York]], and moved with his family to [[Terre Haute, Indiana]] at age nine.{{cite news |url=http://www.tribstar.com/news/local_story_221233524.html?keyword=topstory |title=Greg Oden, the NBA's top pick, returns home to Terre Haute |date=August 9, 2007 |author=David Hughes |newspaper=[[Tribune-Star]] |access-date=August 25, 2008 |archive-date=October 17, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017232741/http://tribstar.com/local/x1155704853/Greg-Oden-the-NBA-s-top-pick-returns-home-to-Terre-Haute?keyword=topstory |url-status=dead }} He attended Sarah Scott Middle School in Terre Haute, where he first played interscholastic basketball. Oden then relocated with his mother and brother and attended [[Lawrence North High School]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]], which he led to three consecutive Indiana Class 4A basketball championships before graduating in 2006. Oden was named [[Parade (magazine)|''Parade'']]'s [[High school (North America)|High School]] Co-Player of the Year 2005 (along with [[Monta Ellis]]) and 2005 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|National Boys Basketball Player of the Year]]. He repeated as Gatorade National Boys Basketball Player of the Year in 2006. Oden was also named the [[Indiana "Mr. Basketball" award|2006 Indiana Mr. Basketball]]. He was also on the [[McDonald's All-American]] Team and played in the All-American game, and earned first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|'' Parade'' All-American]] honors for the second straight year. ==College career== On June 29, 2005, Oden and Lawrence North teammate [[Mike Conley Jr.]] announced that they would be attending [[Ohio State University]] starting with the 2006–07 season. On June 16, 2006, Oden had surgery on his right wrist in Indianapolis to repair a ligament injury that occurred late in his senior high school season.{{Cite web | url=http://ohiostate.scout.com/2/540039.html | title=Oden Facing Wrist Surgery; OSU Hosts Camp | first=Kyle | last=Lamb | date=June 15, 2006 | access-date=May 11, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029084312/http://ohiostate.scout.com/2/540039.html | archive-date=October 29, 2013 | url-status=dead }} As a result, Oden sat on the Ohio State bench during the beginning of the 2006–07 season, during which the Buckeyes were ranked as high as #1 before losing to [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. He made his college debut on December 2, 2006, against [[Valparaiso Crusaders basketball|Valparaiso]], coming off the bench. Oden finished the game with 14 points, 10 rebounds, and five blocks. In December of that year, [[Steve Kerr]] described him as a "once-in-a-decade player".{{cite news |last=Kerr |first=Steve |author-link=Steve Kerr |title=Questions and The Answer |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |date=December 15, 2006 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=sk-mailbag121506&prov=yhoo&type=lgns |access-date=January 29, 2007 }} The Big Ten honored Oden as ''Player of the Week'', along with [[Wisconsin Badgers|Wisconsin]]'s [[Alando Tucker]], on January 29, 2007. In the previous week, he had averaged 18 points and 11.5 rebounds.{{cite news |title=Oden Earns First Big Ten Weekly Award |publisher=Ohio State University Department of Athletics |date=January 29, 2007 |url=http://ohiostatebuckeyes.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/012907aaa.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120717102513/http://ohiostatebuckeyes.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/012907aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 17, 2012 |access-date=January 29, 2007 }} On March 6, 2007, Oden was named First Team All-[[Big Ten]] as well being voted the conference's Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite news|title=Oden to named First Team All-Big Ten, Defensive Player of the Year|date=March 6, 2007|access-date=September 24, 2009|publisher=BigTen.org|url=http://bigten.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030607aad.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090401153650/http://bigten.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030607aad.html|archive-date=April 1, 2009|url-status=dead}} Going into the NCAA Tournament, Ohio State was viewed as heavy favorites due mostly to the efforts of Oden viewed as a consensus top player along with Kevin Durant.{{Cite web|url=http://research.ebsco.com/linkprocessor/plink?id=dac89636-22e2-3d62-947b-def7f9ac823f|title="It's Time for the Bigs to Dance."|date=March 2007|last=DeCourcy|first=Mike}} Oden fouled out for the first time in his college career against [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, and was bothered by foul trouble throughout the tournament. In the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet Sixteen]], Oden blocked a potential game-winning shot in the final seconds against Tennessee to preserve an 85–84 victory and went on to lead Ohio State past Memphis and Georgetown to advance to the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|2007 National Championship]]. In the title game, Oden scored 25 points and had 12 rebounds and four blocked shots in a losing effort against the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. Oden, alongside [[Kevin Durant]], [[Arron Afflalo]], [[Alando Tucker]], and [[Acie Law]] were named to the [[Associated Press]] [[2007 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] Team. Oden and Durant were the first freshmen voted to the All-American First Team since 1990, and the third and fourth overall. Throughout his high school and college career, Oden never lost a home game.{{cite news|title=Oden extras (updated)|first=Jason|last=Quick|publisher=[[OregonLive.com]]|access-date=September 24, 2009|date=May 26, 2007|url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2007/05/oden_extras.html}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2007–2012)=== [[File:Greg Oden Comic-Con 2008.jpg|thumb|left|Oden at the 2008 [[San Diego Comic-Con]]]] On April 20, 2007, Oden announced that he would be entering the [[2007 NBA draft]]. Oden was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the #1 overall pick. To begin his Trail Blazers career, Oden chose the uniform number 52. On July 1, before his first NBA practice, Oden was signed to a [[contract]] which provided for two guaranteed seasons and team options for third and fourth seasons. On September 14, 2007, Oden had [[microfracture surgery]] on his ailing right knee. He missed the entire season.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3017538 |title=Oden's recovery from surgery likely in range of 6–12 months |date=September 14, 2007 |work=ESPN.com |access-date=November 19, 2007}} Oden's progress was recorded on the Trail Blazers' website and his [[blog]]. Although drafted in 2007, Oden was classified as a rookie for the 2008–09 season because of the knee injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=thorpe_david&page=Rookies-080627|title=Rookie Watch: Who are the early favorites for ROY?|date=June 27, 2008|first=David|last=Thorpe|access-date=September 24, 2009|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} Entering the 2008–09 season, he was listed at {{convert|250|lbs|abbr=on}}, but according to Blazers' trainer Jay Jensen, Oden weighed about {{convert|290|lbs|abbr=on}} in July.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/greg_oden/ |title=Greg Oden Info Page |work=Players |publisher=NBA.com |access-date=July 26, 2008}}{{cite news |title=Big man's small step |date=August 5, 2008 |first=Jason |last=Quick |publisher=oregonlive.com |access-date=January 18, 2009 |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/oregonian/index.ssf?/base/sports/121790850650380.xml&coll=7 |archive-date=August 30, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080830224937/http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/oregonian/index.ssf?/base/sports/121790850650380.xml&coll=7 |url-status=dead }} Oden left his NBA debut with a foot injury after playing thirteen scoreless minutes against the Los Angeles Lakers.{{cite web |title=Blazers' Oden leaves game early with foot injury |work=NBA.com |access-date=January 18, 2009 |url=http://www.nba.com/2008/news/10/29/odeninjury.ap/index.html?rss=true |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121109212958/http://www.nba.com/2008/news/10/29/odeninjury.ap/index.html?rss=true |archive-date=November 9, 2012 |url-status=dead }} He returned on November 12, 2008, after missing two weeks, and scored his first NBA points in the first quarter against the Miami Heat. On January 19, 2009, Oden had a career-high 24 points while also grabbing 15 rebounds in a 102–85 victory over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |title=Bucks 85, Trail Blazers 102 |work=ESPN.com |access-date=January 19, 2009 |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290119022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090123025250/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290119022|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 23, 2009}} On February 13, 2009, he injured his left knee in a game against the [[Golden State Warriors]], by bumping knees with opponent [[Corey Maggette]], and missed three weeks due to a chipped knee cap. [[File: Greg Oden Wizards.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Oden dunking in a game against the Washington Wizards]] On November 23, 2009, Oden matched his career-high for points in a game again with 24. He set a new career-high for rebounds in a game with 20 on December 1. Four days later, Oden injured his left knee in the first quarter of a game. He was taken off the court on two connected stretchers. Later, Oden underwent surgery for a fractured left [[patella]] and missed the rest of the season. That injury marked the second time Oden had missed major playing time due to injury.{{cite news|url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5gYPtOsRksnU-CbLODkwMQ-c4KecQD9CE66980|title=Oden tells teammates to keep fighting without him|agency=Associated Press|access-date=December 6, 2009|date=December 7, 2009}}{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} On November 17, 2010, the team announced that Oden would have microfracture surgery on his left knee, ending his 2010–11 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2010/11/breaking_news_blazers_greg_ode.html|title=Breaking news: Blazers Greg Oden faces another microfracture surgery|date=November 17, 2010|work=[[The Oregonian]]|publisher=OregonLive.com|access-date=November 18, 2010}} The injury marked Oden's third NBA season cut short due to a knee injury. On December 9, 2011, the Trail Blazers announced that Oden had suffered an unspecified "setback" that left them less optimistic about his ability to play in the 2011–12 season. Rather than signing an $8.9 million [[qualifying offer]], Oden and the team negotiated a different offer.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7336972/trail-blazers-greg-oden-suffers-setback-signs-reduced-deal-portland|title=Oden done}} On February 3, 2012, he underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right knee.{{cite news| url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2012/02/trail_blazers_center_greg_oden_to_undergo_yet_anot.html | work=The Oregonian | title=Trail Blazers center Greg Oden undergoes "successful" knee surgery today | date=February 3, 2012}} On February 20, Oden was scheduled for a procedure on his left knee similar to the procedure he underwent 17 days earlier. However, during the operation, further damage to the [[Hyaline cartilage|articular cartilage]] was discovered, and Oden underwent his third micro-fracture surgery.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7595246/surgery-greg-oden-portland-trail-blazers-turned-third-microfracture |title=Greg Oden has microfracture surgery |date=February 20, 2012 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} On March 15, 2012, Oden was waived by the Trail Blazers to create room on the roster for trade acquisitions.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7692811/portland-trail-blazers-waive-former-no-1-overall-pick-greg-oden|title=Blazers waive center Greg Oden|work=ESPN.com|date=March 15, 2012 |access-date=April 25, 2016}} In May 2012, Oden announced his intention to sit out the 2012–13 season to focus on rehabbing his injuries.{{cite web|url=http://www.grantland.com/story/_/id/7908766/a-rare-interview-former-no-1-overall-pick-greg-oden-injury-plagued-career|title=Oden on Oden|author=Mark Titus|work=Grantland|access-date=April 25, 2016}} In January 2013, it was reported that several teams were interested in signing Oden for the 2013–14 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8832157/greg-oden-former-no-1-overall-pick-plans-resume-playing-career-sources|title=Sources: Greg Oden plans to return|work=ESPN.com|date=January 10, 2013 |access-date=April 25, 2016}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8898371/sources-greg-oden-drawing-interest-more-miami-heat-cleveland-cavaliers|title=Sources: Greg Oden draws interest|work=ESPN.com|date=January 30, 2013 |access-date=April 25, 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://nesn.com/2013/02/report-greg-oden-meets-with-celtics-to-discuss-potential-signing/|title=Report: Greg Oden Meets With Celtics to Discuss Potential Signing|work=NESN.com|date=February 2, 2013 |access-date=April 25, 2016}} ===Miami Heat (2013–2014)=== On August 7, 2013, Oden signed a one-year deal with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news_recap/heat-signs-greg-oden | title=HEAT Signs Greg Oden | work=NBA.com | date=August 7, 2013 | access-date=August 7, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://nba.si.com/2013/08/14/greg-oden-miami-heat-one-year-contract/|title=Agent: Greg Oden only signed one-year deal with Heat|work=SI.com|date=August 14, 2013|access-date=August 23, 2013}} He played in his first NBA game since December 5, 2009, in a preseason game against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on October 23, 2013. Oden managed to score two points through a dunk attempt and grabbed two rebounds in four minutes of play.{{cite web|title=James, Wade lead Heat over Pelicans, 108–95|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400491591|work=ESPN.com|date=October 23, 2013|access-date=October 28, 2013}} On January 15, 2014, Oden made his long-awaited return to the court. In his first regular-season game since December 2009, he recorded six points and two rebounds in eight minutes during a 114–97 loss to the Washington Wizards.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140115/MIAWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Heat at Wizards|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140119030151/http://www.nba.com/games/20140115/MIAWAS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 19, 2014|url-status=dead}} On February 23, Oden made his first start since December 2009 in the Heat's 93–79 win over the Chicago Bulls. He played in three playoff games in that year. The Heat made the [[2014 NBA Finals]] where they faced the [[San Antonio Spurs]]; Oden played a minute each in Game 3 and Game 4, recording only a personal foul in the latter. The Heat went on to lose the series in five games.{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/odengr01/gamelog-playoffs/ | title=Greg Oden Playoffs Game Log }} === Jiangsu Dragons (2015–2016) === In March 2015, Oden was reported to be working out with the Memphis Grizzlies, while he also returned to his alma mater, Ohio State, to undergo some "high-level training" with [[Thad Matta]], then Ohio State basketball team coach. Matta stated that since September 2014, Oden had been working out with the other Ohio State coaches. In June 2015, Oden had workouts with the Charlotte Hornets and the Dallas Mavericks. He told the media that he was attempting an NBA comeback with plans to return to the league for the 2016–17 season.{{Cite web |date=June 21, 2015 |title=Greg Oden comeback: Former Miami Heat center has two workouts |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2015/06/21/greg-oden-comeback-nba-team-workouts |access-date=April 25, 2016 |website=SI.com}} On August 26, 2015, Oden signed a one-year, $1.2 million contract with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite news |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/173893/greg-oden-passes-the-tryout-period-jiangsu-dragons-sign-him.html |title=Greg Oden passes the tryout period. Jiangsu Dragons sign him |work=Sportando.com |date=August 26, 2015 |access-date=August 26, 2015}} On December 9, he recorded a season-high 22 points and 14 rebounds in a win over [[Shandong Golden Stars|Shandong]].{{cite web |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid/CHN/ot/1/pid/6043881/season/2016/tid/6025010/playerView.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308214154/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid/CHN/ot/1/pid/6043881/season/2016/tid/6025010/playerView.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 8, 2016 |title=Greg Oden | Season 2015/2016 |work=FIBA.com |access-date=January 15, 2016}} On February 1, 2016, Oden parted ways with Jiangsu.{{cite news|title=Jiangsu waive Greg Oden, offer Marshon Brooks a two-year contract extension|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/189652/jiangsu-waive-greg-oden-offer-marshon-brooks-a-two-year-contract-extension.html|access-date=February 1, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=February 1, 2016}} In 25 games for the club, he averaged 13 points, 12.6 rebounds, and two blocks per game.{{cite news|last=Lesmerises|first=Doug|title=Cut in China, back in Columbus, former Buckeye Greg Oden talks about his basketball future|url=http://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2016/02/cut_in_china_back_in_columbus.html|access-date=February 11, 2016|work=Cleveland.com|date=February 9, 2016}} In July 2018, Oden agreed to play as a reserve with the Scarlet & Gray, a team of Ohio State alumni who competed in [[The Basketball Tournament 2018]], a $2 million winner-take-all summer tournament.{{cite news |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2018/07/scarlet_gray_add_greg_oden_los.html |title=Scarlet & Gray add Greg Oden, lose Jared Sullinger and Byron Mullens: The Basketball Tournament preview, TV info |website=cleveland.com |date=July 27, 2018 |access-date=July 27, 2018}} Oden made his debut for Scarlet & Gray on July 27,{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/video/clip?id=24213732 |title=Oden backs his way in for first TBT layup |website=[[ESPN]] |date=July 27, 2018 |access-date=July 27, 2018}} scoring 11 points in 16 minutes of playing time.{{cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/news/1-scarlet-gray-downs-12-primetime-players-72-60 |title=#1 Scarlet & Gray Downs #12 Primetime Players 72-60 |website=thetournament.com |url-status=dead }} ==Post-playing career== On April 12, 2016, Oden was hired by the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team]] to be the student manager for the team while he went back to finish his degree at the college.{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2016/04/greg_odens_role_as_student_man.html|title=Greg Oden's role as a student manager with Ohio State basketball, and Thad Matta's debt to a former player|work=cleveland.com|date=April 22, 2016 |access-date=April 25, 2016}} In 2019, Oden graduated from Ohio State with a bachelor's degree in [[sport industry]].{{cite web|first1=Phil|last1=Harrison|url=https://buckeyeswire.usatoday.com/2019/05/06/former-ohio-state-big-man-greg-oden-officially-graduates/|title=Former Ohio State big man Greg Oden officially graduates|date=May 6, 2019|work=usatoday.com|access-date=May 6, 2019}} On November 21, 2019, Edyoucore Sports & Entertainment announced that Oden had joined
